mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and depressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the observed mean return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.2 million units signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the cumulative return is not significantly below the median baseline at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals persistent labor market slack, reducing corporate earnings expectations and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% alongside a concurrent drop in real retail sales (RSAFS) below $650 billion signals contraction in manufacturing and retail demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 2.0% in response to a financial shock signals accommodative policy, lowering risk-free rates and boosting present value of corporate cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops below 2.0% in a single month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise of more than 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall of more than 2% in industrial production (INDPRO) within a single month signals a synchronized labor-supply and output contraction, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE change > 0.4pp AND INDPRO change < -2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative in triggered months at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS change > 200000 for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 0.5% for three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically boosts corporate revenues and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change > 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods at 5% significance.
